entries.message: Fix - Force live sync on manual unwatch and wait for it to finish before the UI shows the new state
entries.author: Lasikiewicz
details: Manual unwatch (single episode, season/show bulk, and clearing Part Watched progress) now forces a live re-push to Plex, Emby, Jellyfin, and Trakt even when Plembfin's own database already shows the item unwatched, matching the mark-watched fix from the previous commit
Automated paths (webhooks, the scheduler, tracker sync) keep their original loop-protection skip, since that guard is what stops their own echoes from re-dispatching forever

Mark watched no longer flips an episode, season, or movie to "watched" the instant you click it - it now shows "Syncing..." and only updates once the live sync to every connected app has actually finished
The manual-watch API now waits for that sync to complete before responding, instead of dispatching it in the background and reporting an unverified queued count
Documented both changes in docs/media-detail.md

entries.message: Fix - Force a live resync when marking a season or show watched that plembfin already has as watched
entries.author: Lasikiewicz
details: Mark season watched / Mark Watched (show) no longer silently skips episodes plembfin's own history already shows as watched - they're re-pushed to Plex, Emby, Jellyfin, and Trakt in the same batch, using their existing watched date so history isn't rewritten
Fixes a drift bug where a media server that lost its watched flag after the original sync (e.g. following a library rescan) stayed unwatched forever unless the user ran Force Sync manually
When a season or the whole show has nothing left unwatched, the button relabels to "Resync season" / "Resync Watched" instead of disabling, so it stays usable for exactly this case
Documented the new resync behavior in docs/media-detail.md

entries.message: Fix - Recover Trakt dispatch when a media server reports a wrong episode id
entries.author: Lasikiewicz
details: Fixed a real incident: Force Sync failed to mark Reacher S02E02 watched on Trakt (not_found) because the stored record's provider ids - reported by a real Plex webhook scrobble, not derived by Plembfin - didn't correspond to any real show; S02E01 in the same run succeeded only because it had no per-episode id and naturally fell back to the show's correct one

Episode writes already skip resolving series-level ids once an episode carries any id of its own, since that id normally must win over a title-based guess - this meant a media server's own mismatched match for one specific episode was never given a second look

Trakt dispatch now retries once with the show's own known series ids, but only after Trakt has explicitly rejected the episode's stored id with not_found - a working id is never speculatively second-guessed, only one Trakt has already refused
A recovered dispatch reports that the show's series id was used instead of a bare success, so this stays visible instead of silently masking the underlying bad episode id

entries.message: Fix - Close a gap where an identity-poor already-watched episode could still be duplicated
entries.author: Lasikiewicz
details: Fixed a real gap in the duplicate-watch safeguard: it only ran the thorough watch-history identity check when the faster playstate check already agreed the item was watched, so a record old enough to predate provider-id tracking (title-only key) could slip past both and still get duplicated

Verified live: Reacher S01E01 (a properly identified, IMDb-keyed episode) was correctly protected, but School Spirits S03E04 (a title-only legacy record) let three duplicate marks through in a row before this fix

Both watch-state checks now run independently rather than one gated behind the other, so an item is treated as already watched if either finds it - closing the gap for any similarly old record library-wide, not just this one episode
Cleaned up the duplicates created during testing via Remove Duplicate Watches; no lasting data changes from this investigation

entries.message: Fix - Stop mark-watched from ever creating a duplicate on an already-watched item
entries.author: Lasikiewicz
details: Fixed a real incident: School Spirits kept accumulating duplicate watch records - a season page left open for ~20 minutes stopped reflecting a batch mark-watched that happened elsewhere, and clicking Mark Watched on what the stale page still showed as unwatched logged a second play for an episode the server already had watched

Manual mark-watched and marking watched from Part Watched now check the item's actual current watch state before inserting, not just whether a row exists at the exact timestamp the request happens to use - an item the server already has watched is reported as already-logged instead of getting a second play recorded, no matter how stale the page that submitted the request was

Cleaned up the duplicates already live on production: Remove Duplicate Watches removed 16 duplicate TV watches across 9 episodes library-wide and pushed the corrected state to every connected platform

entries.message: Fix - Stop non-release commits from polluting changelog entries
entries.author: Lasikiewicz
details: Fixed a real problem: the v0.8.6 release notes were dumping bullets from a chore commit (an internal debug-only endpoint) and a test commit (fixing test expectations) into the same entry as real feature and bug-fix work, making Settings -> Changelog read like a raw commit log instead of release notes

The changelog generator now only backfills bullets from commits typed feat, fix, security, enhance, perf, or docs - a chore/test/refactor/style/ci commit bundled into the same push never contributes its own bullets, even when it isn't otherwise CI plumbing
Applies to both the main and alpha changelog generators, which share the same filtering logic
Manually cleaned the noise already published in the current v0.8.6 and v0.8.3 entries so what's live in Settings -> Changelog reads correctly now, not just for future releases

Also removed one bullet that was pure investigation narration with no resulting product change (a bug report that turned out to be a stale session, not a code fix) - the type filter can't catch this since it lived inside an otherwise legitimate feature commit
